newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus stocks remain low in muted trading.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus stocks remain low in muted trading.

text.p: Cyprus stocks entered the New Year hovering at low trading levels but selective stocks in the banking and trading sector are expected to do well, analysts said.
"We are starting at a low base," said Stavros Agrotis at CISCO, the Cyprus Investment and Securities Corporation.
"In 1997 we should see a rise in selective stocks like banks and trading companies but (overall) I don't see a downside risk," he said.
The Cyprus Stock Exchange (CSE) 41-share general index closed at 82.15 on Friday, dropping 0.18 percent from last week's closing figure of 82.30.
Banking shares showed little movement, with their sectoral index closing at 91.68 from 91.69.
Fully paid shares in Bank of Cyprus closed at 344 cents, slipping one cent from last week. Fully paid shares of Cyprus Popular Bank closed at 330.5 cents, sliding three cents.
Hellenic Bank closed at 264.5, up four cents from last week. Shares in Universal Savings Bank climbed 5.5 cents to close at 138.5.
Approved investment stocks climbed one percent higher, closing at 74.52. Shares in Era Portfolio Investments went up two cents, closing at 130.5. Cytrustees shares closed at 152 from 150 last week.
Insurance stocks went up in the week but settled back to 57.79 on Friday from 57.63 last week.

Universal Life shares went up 4.5 cents, closing at 369. Paneuropean Insurance fully paid gained 2.5 cents, closing at 123.5. Interamerican Insurance fully paid went up 1.5 cents, closing at 106.5. Philiki Insurance fully paid dropped 14.5 cents, closing at 216.
Cement producer Vassiliko closed at 160, down 4 cents. Beer and wine producer Keo went up two cents to close at 115.5.
National carrier Cyprus Airways closed at 35.5 cents from 35.8 cents last Friday.
On Monday it fell to its lowest level in 1996, to 35.1 cents.
